clue.text: Send up a firework that finally explodes

definitions.meaning: to send up is to lampoon, and a satirical lampoon or the act of writing one is this
a small firework that fizzes and hisses before going off with a bang

explanation.surface: Someone launches a rocket that bursts at the end of its flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a short satirical attack and a small hissing banger, so it covers lampooning and the firework.

clue.text: Drunk having rounds at The Crown, as it were

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard
Os are round letters
the crown of a hill is its summit or peak

explanation.surface: A drinker is buying rounds at a pub called The Crown, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Crown' looks like a pub name, but it is the top of something, a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A filler phrase used to flag that words are meant loosely, in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Dishevelled politician during feast, losing head

indicators.note: the politician comes during, inside, the feast word
the first letter of the feast word is dropped

parts.note: a junket is a feast or jaunt
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP looks a mess at a banquet after losing his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' leaves UNKET, which 'during' opens up; a junket is a lavish feast, often at public expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkempt hair or clothes are untidy and messy.

clue.text: Instrument used in bar work, mostly

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the work word goes

parts.note: a job is work

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is played during most of a shift in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub; it is the verb to forbid. 'mostly' drops the B from JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed instrument with a drum-like body.

clue.text: Nothing in Shakespeare's play directors have to discuss here?

indicators.note: nothing sits inside the playwright's nickname, so the zero goes in

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare's familiar title
nothing is zero, the letter O
play means room, as in scope to move

explanation.surface: A drama critic notes that nothing in a Shakespeare play is up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shakespeare's play' reads as the title of one of his works, but splits in two; 'in' places the zero inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Company directors meet and debate in a dedicated chamber, so the question describes where their meetings happen.

clue.text: Light-hearted report of youth worker

indicators.note: report of means we hear the phrase spoken

parts.note: a youth is a boy and a worker is an ant

explanation.surface: A cheerful account is given of a youth worker.
explanation.walkthrough: BOY plus ANT, said together, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant spirits are cheerful and resilient.

clue.text: Silver, say, in which half our capital's invested over considerable time

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, as money is put in

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say

indicators.note: half takes the first half of the city's name

parts.note: for a British paper our capital is London

explanation.surface: A financier puts half the City's silver into an investment for the long haul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'our capital' assumes a British reader; 'half' cuts the city to its first three letters, which 'invested' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Agelong means lasting for ages, so it describes something enduring a very long time.

clue.text: Notice girl being embraced by two others

parts.note: Di is a girl's name

indicators.note: the girl is held inside the pair of names

parts.note: Sal is another girl's name
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman is given notice while two colleagues hug her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two others' means two more girls' names; 'being embraced by' places the girl inside them, splitting the second name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given one's notice means being sacked, a dismissal from a job.

clue.text: Veteran great painter scholar overlooked

indicators.note: overlooked means left out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an old master is a great European painter
MA is a Master of Arts, a scholar

explanation.surface: A distinguished elderly artist is passed over by the academic.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing MA from OLD MASTER leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an old person, someone long in the tooth.

clue.text: American spotted after thirty seconds or less

indicators.note: spotted means placed, so the American comes after

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, so half that word, its first three letters

explanation.surface: An American is seen in half a minute or under.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so half that word stands for it; 'spotted after' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means reduced by, as in ten take away two, so it stands for less.

clue.text: Parliamentary figure provisionally agreed to start discussion

definitions.text: Parliamentary figure provisionally agreed to start discussion

parts.words: Parliamentary figure provisionally agreed to start discussion
parts.note: describes a nominal sum put to the Commons so that a supply debate can begin, the real amount being settled later

explanation.surface: An MP is provisionally approved to open a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a person in Parliament, but it is a sum of money: a nominal amount voted so that discussion of an estimate can start.
explanation.definitionFit: In Commons procedure a nominal amount is voted on as a placeholder, allowing a debate before the full estimate is approved.

clue.text: American car seen in French town

definitions.meaning: the US word for a saloon car
a town in the Ardennes, scene of the 1870 battle

explanation.surface: A big Yankee motor is spotted in a provincial French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a four-door saloon by this name, and it is also a town on the Meuse in northern France.

clue.text: South. American boy, worries about heading for trouble — it's a tragedy

parts.note: Uncle Sam personifies America
a boy is a son

indicators.note: the worries word wraps around the other letters

parts.note: worries are agonies

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here of trouble

explanation.surface: An American boy from the South frets about trouble ahead, and it all ends in tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ST (S for South plus T from 'heading for trouble') inside AGONIES. Though printed first, South goes inside the worries, not at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's closet drama about the blinded Hebrew strongman is written as a classical tragedy.

clue.text: Area no longer producing milk?

parts.note: ex- means former, no longer so
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A field has dried up and no longer gives milk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a dairy pasture gone dry; in fact 'milk' is a verb meaning to draw out.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk something is to draw out or obtain from it, which is what this verb means.

clue.text: Acknowledgment of commercial undertaking

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, an ad
a mission is a task or undertaking

explanation.surface: A firm acknowledges a business venture.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a confession, owning up to something.

clue.text: Like a tummy upset son got in awfully tragic case

indicators.note: the son's letter gets inside the rearranged word
awfully suggests the word tragic is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy has caught a dreadful stomach bug and is a sorry sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns TRAGIC into GATRIC, and 'got in' places S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastric means relating to the stomach, so a tummy upset is a gastric complaint.

clue.text: Hook it, as batsman might do

definitions.meaning: in cricket, play a cut shot and then take a run

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to flee hastily, and literally describes a cricket stroke, the cut, followed by a run.

clue.text: Spot of trouble abroad, taking money, say, over border

indicators.note: say tells us the word for money is to be spoken and spelt as it sounds

parts.note: cash is money

indicators.note: over in a down-reading sense here means the edge word is turned back

parts.note: a rim is a border

explanation.surface: Trouble overseas is put down to cash being smuggled over a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the border word backwards. 'Spot of trouble' is a trouble spot: the disputed region between India and Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan region contested by India and Pakistan is a long-running flashpoint overseas.

clue.text: Act passed to restrict union, say

indicators.note: to restrict means to hold in, so the union letters are enclosed

parts.note: to state is to say
TU is a trade union

explanation.surface: A law is passed to curb the trade unions, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb STATE, holding TU (trade union).
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Make an impression again on children

parts.note: re means on, regarding
issue means offspring

explanation.surface: Someone tries again to impress the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an impression' looks social but means to print again.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue a book is to print a fresh run of it.

clue.text: Canvass in politics poorly after ditching leader

indicators.note: poorly suggests the remaining letters are arranged badly into a new word
the leading letter of politics is dropped

explanation.surface: A campaigner does badly in politics after the party drops its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching leader' removes the P of POLITICS to leave OLITICS, which 'poorly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit votes or support is to canvass for them.

clue.text: Inputs encrypted on computer unit in spacecraft

indicators.note: encrypted suggests the letters are scrambled into code

parts.note: K is a kilobyte, a unit of computer memory

explanation.surface: Coded inputs are entered into a computer aboard a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encrypted' rearranges INPUTS into SPUTNI, followed by K.
explanation.definitionFit: Sputnik was the first artificial satellite, launched by the Soviet Union in 1957.

clue.text: Cheerful, smartly dressed golfer approaching green

definitions.meaning: one who plays a short lofted shot onto the putting surface

explanation.surface: A golfer approaching the green is cheery and well turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means bright and spruce; as a noun it names a player making a short pitch shot.

clue.text: A total change, possibly, for us at training

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A coach promises a complete makeover for the squad at training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles the fifteen letters of FOR US AT TRAINING.
explanation.definitionFit: A transfiguration is a complete transformation of form or appearance.

clue.text: Name American, combination that has banks in Iberia

parts.note: a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: An American name is joined to a combination lock at an Iberian bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'banks' are riverbanks, not financial houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian peninsula, flowing to the sea at Lisbon.

clue.text: Drink the old man knocked over in alarm

indicators.note: knocked over means turned on its back, reading backwards

parts.note: to lap is to drink
pa is dad, the old man

explanation.surface: Dad's drink is knocked over, causing alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns LAPPA backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or dismay deeply.

clue.text: Good, and mostly sound, Spanish architect

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: audio means sound

explanation.surface: A Spanish architect is praised as good and largely sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the final O from AUDIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoni Gaudí designed the Sagrada Família in Barcelona.

clue.text: Polish article written by Chopin's friend

parts.note: the novelist George Sand was Chopin's companion
a paper is a written article

explanation.surface: A piece about the composer is penned by his famous companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality, echoing Chopin, but it is the verb to smooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive paper is used to smooth and polish wood.

clue.text: Novelist given stick, having been badly reviewed

indicators.note: badly reviewed hints the letters are looked over again in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A writer takes flak after a poor notice from the critics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly reviewed' rearranges STICK and BEEN; 'given' and 'having' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: John Steinbeck was the American author of The Grapes of Wrath.

clue.text: Advance after installing right navigational aid

indicators.note: the loan word takes the right letter inside it

parts.note: an advance is a loan

explanation.surface: A firm offers credit once the right kit has been fitted for navigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Loran is a long-range radio positioning system used by ships and aircraft.
